chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd, from Yūnus, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

"Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام cut [the thief's hand] for an egg." He said: I said, "And what is an egg?" So he said, "An egg whose value is a quarter of a dīnār." He said: I said, "It is the lowest limit of the thief," so he remained silent.

key_terms.أَدْنَى حَدِّ السَّارِقِ: the lowest limit at which the thief is subject to the legal hadd
key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amīr al-Muʾminīn, Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.بَيْضَةٍ: an egg; here explained as an item valued at a quarter of a dīnār
key_terms.رُبُعُ دِينَارٍ: one quarter of a dīnār, the stated threshold amount

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum value at which the hadd punishment for theft is applied in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام enforced the hadd for theft in the case of an item valued at a quarter of a dīnār. The report indicates that this amount represents the minimum threshold for the thief, and it pertains to legal rulings concerning theft and judicial punishment.
